He grew up in the Crusader states and learned the politics of the region. *Early Life and Inheritance* describes his upbringing and the responsibilities he assumed as a young count.

He married Eschiva of Bures a noblewoman from the northern territories of the Kingdom of Jerusalem. The marriage strengthened ties with local lords but produced no male heir. He also maintained relations with the King of Jerusalem and with the Byzantine Empire through diplomatic envoys. *Political Alliances and Conflicts* covers his shifting loyalties during the reigns of Baldwin IV Baldwin V and Guy of Lusignan. He often opposed Guy's rise to power and supported the claim of Isabella and Humphrey of Toron. His rivalry with Guy culminated in the tense period before the Battle of Hattin where Raymond commanded a contingent of troops but withdrew from the field after disagreements with the royal command.

After the disastrous defeat at Hattin in 1187 Raymond was captured by Saladin forces. He spent his final months in captivity where he fell ill and died. His death marked the end of direct rule by his line in Tripoli and the county passed to his sister's son Raymond of Antioch. *Later Years and Death* details his imprisonment his final days and the impact of his loss on the Crusader states. His legacy is remembered as that of a prudent lord who tried to balance Muslim pressure with Crusader unity though his inability to secure a successor weakened the region."
